lessons.title: Inventions are great!
lessons.kind: 对话 · 刘老师与同学们讨论最重要的发明
canonical: Today, let’s discuss inventions and their roles in shaping our world. Which invention do you think is the most important?
I believe the invention of paper has greatly influenced the development of human civilization.
How about the telephone? It allows people to communicate with each other easily and quickly.
The light bulb is also an important invention. It lights up the world.
I think washing machines are helpful inventions, and both electric and gas-powered cars are cool.
These are all very good examples! Are there any other inventions coming to your mind?
Computers are very important. People can do so much on a computer.
And don’t forget about the internet! It connects people from all over the world and provides us with information, knowledge, and entertainment.

lessons.title: Ways of travelling
lessons.kind: 说明文 · 从轮子到宇宙飞船，人类交通方式的演变
canonical: Long ago, people did not travel far from home. In fact, in the early days, a person might live their whole life in one village and never travel far.
The first important invention in travel was the wheel. And then came the wagons. Humans began to have the power to move and carry things across long distances.
The next was the train. After the train came the invention of cars, buses, trucks, and other means of transportation.
Humans and goods were able to travel farther than ever before.
Boats and ships provided another important way of travelling. The invention of the compass helped people explore more places.
And canal systems made fast waterway transportation possible.
Modern means of transportation, such as high-speed trains and airplanes, help people travel faster and farther.
Eco-friendly electric cars are common and self-driving cars are in development. People can even travel to space in spaceships. Who knows what the future holds?
The development of transportation has made people’s travel much easier and faster. Every invention is a symbol of human creativity.
Let’s enjoy these developments and work for more great things in the future.

lessons.title: Computers and the internet
lessons.kind: 对话 · 珍妮和妈妈聊电脑与互联网给学习带来的变化
canonical: Jenny wants to do her homework on the computer. But her mum is using it.
Mum, is it okay if I use the computer now?
Okay. I just finished my work, so it’s all yours. Jenny, you’re so lucky to have a computer.
Yes, I am. As it’s connected to the internet, it has made study and research much easier.
This technology helps students a lot with their homework. But when I was a student, computers were not widely used. And the internet was not as convenient as it is now.
I couldn’t imagine having such a convenient tool for getting the job done.
Mum, how was homework done in those days?
Well, everything was written by hand on paper. When I didn’t know how to spell a word, I had to look it up in a printed dictionary.
When I needed to do any research, I had to go to the library.
But now with the internet we can simply search for everything online. And there’s always new technology, like AI.
Yes, and you can easily find definitions and examples for any word. The internet and the computer are amazing inventions with many applications.
I agree with you on that, Mum.

lessons.title: Thank you, Mr Pasteur!
lessons.kind: 对话 · 杰瑞米和妈妈聊牛奶的巴氏杀菌与巴斯德
canonical: While pouring a glass of milk, Jeremy notices something written on the package.
Hey, Mum! I just noticed a big word on the carton. PASTEURIZED. What does it mean?
Well, if something is pasteurized, it means that it has gone through a process of heating to a certain temperature.
Why do we heat milk?
Raw milk has dangerous bacteria and germs. We must heat milk to 72 degrees Celsius for 15 seconds to kill them.
How did people discover that?
Many years ago, people sometimes got sick when they drank milk. Some of them even died because of the bad bacteria.
Wow! Who discovered this heating process? A dairy farmer or a scientist?
It was Louis Pasteur, a French microbiologist. He discovered the process around 1864.
That’s a long time ago!
Mr Pasteur was one of the greatest scientists. His work saved millions of lives around the world. He was famous for his work on germs.
Well, here’s a toast to you, Mr Pasteur. Thank you for making the world much safer.

lessons.title: Refrigerator timeline
lessons.kind: 时间线说明文 · 从古代冰藏到节能冰箱的发展
canonical: Ancient times: Ancient China, Greece, and Rome used ice or snow to preserve food by freezing or chilling it.
1600s: Icehouses were used to preserve food all year-round.
1748: William Cullen did an experiment on artificial refrigeration.
1805: Oliver Evans designed the first refrigeration machine.
1890s: Iceboxes became popular. They were smaller icehouses meant for home use.
1913: Fred W. Wolf invented the first home electric refrigerator.
1918: Mass production of home refrigerators began.
1920s: Refrigerators became popular in some countries.
1940s: Freezer compartments were added.
1980s: Water dispensers were added.
1996: Refrigerators became more energy-saving.

lessons.title: Great inventions of ancient China
lessons.kind: 说明文 · 中国古代的算盘、豆腐、制茶与瓷器
canonical: We all know the most significant inventions of ancient China — paper-making, printing, gunpowder, and compasses.
However, Chinese people also made many other fascinating inventions.
Have you used the abacus? It was invented in China over 2,500 years ago. It became the primary tool used by merchants and bankers to calculate.
Tofu originated in China. It is a good source of protein. Tofu is rich in minerals that are important for building strong bones and reducing the risk of some diseases.
It has been an important part of Chinese cuisine for over 2,000 years and is now enjoyed worldwide.
Tea making is another invention from China.
It is said that Shennong, an ancient Chinese emperor, discovered tea when a tea leaf accidentally fell into a pot of boiling water.
Today, tea is popular all over the world.
The origins of porcelain can be traced back to the Han Dynasty in China. Porcelain quickly spread throughout China and reached other parts of the world.
